briefs.headline: Exxon ends the week near $171 after a first-step deal to return to Venezuela
briefs.summary: Exxon stock closed at $170.59 on November 13, and someone who put $1,000 in a year ago would now have about $1,432. On November 9, Exxon signed a non-binding first agreement with Venezuela's state oil company to study seven oil areas, with one year of exclusive talks. Venezuela took Exxon's projects there in 2007, and that fight is still not settled. Oil prices dipped, with Brent crude briefly falling below $90 a barrel on November 10, which can mean lower profits for oil companies.
bull: The Venezuela deal gives Exxon one year of exclusive talks on seven oil areas in a country with huge oil reserves.
Exxon cut its debt by $8 billion last quarter and plans to buy back $20 billion of its own stock in 2027.
Exxon wants to make money even when oil costs only $35 a barrel by 2027, which helps it handle price drops.
bear: The Venezuela deal is not binding, and Exxon says it needs stable rules and good profits before investing.
Oil prices have been falling, with Brent dipping below $90 on November 10, and lower oil prices usually mean lower profits.
One bank, DZ Bank, cut its rating to sell with a $170 price goal, about where the stock trades now.

briefs.headline: J&J closes at a record $283.52 after good drug news and new investments
briefs.summary: Johnson & Johnson stock rose 1.1% to $283.52 on November 12, a new high, and is up about 39% this year. Funds that track big groups of stocks bought about $89.7 million of J&J shares on November 11, their third day of buying in a row. On November 12, J&J led a $100 million investment in Delix Therapeutics, which works on depression medicines, and said it will back Francis Medical's prostate cancer device. Two days earlier, J&J said its drug Caplyta helped adults with bipolar I disorder in a big final-stage test.
bull: Caplyta passed its second big final-stage bipolar test, with 43.9% of patients improving by half or more versus 23.7% on a fake pill.
J&J led a $100 million investment in Delix Therapeutics and is backing a new prostate cancer device, adding possible future products.
The stock hit a new high and is up about 39% this year, and most analysts rate it a buy.
bear: A law firm said on November 12 it is looking into whether J&J misled investors, which is only an investigation but can lead to lawsuits.
Third-quarter profit fell to just $210 million (9 cents a share) because of billions in costs to settle talc baby powder lawsuits.
The stock costs about 42 times its yearly profit, which is expensive for a large, slower-growing company.

briefs.summary: On Friday, November 13, the Dow rose about 50 points, or 0.1%, to 52,347.55, the only major index to end higher. Dow member Nvidia still fell about 2% after its CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and Cisco dropped early even after a strong quarter. The Dow gained about 2% for the week.

briefs.headline: Small companies dip 0.3% Friday as interest rates climb above 5%
briefs.summary: On Friday, November 13, the Russell 2000, which tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies, fell about 0.3% to 2,790.49. It opened down about 1.7% before cutting most of its loss. Smaller companies often borrow more money, so they are hurt when interest rates rise, and the 10-year Treasury rate touched about 5.17% as traders bet on a Fed rate hike in December. This came after a 1.7% drop on Thursday, when small companies fell more than the other big indexes.

bear: The 10-year Treasury rate hit about 5.17%, raising borrowing costs for small companies.

briefs.headline: Micron falls about 5% Friday and is down 20% in a month as chip stocks slide
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory.
briefs.summary: Micron stock fell about 5% to around $760 on November 13 and is down about 20% from $953 a month ago. Chip stocks dropped after Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO of Nvidia, which is Micron's biggest customer, and investors worry that could slow AI spending. This is happening even though business is booming: Micron's last quarter brought in a record $54.23 billion, almost five times more than a year earlier. Some writers say the stock now looks cheap compared with its profits.
bull: Last quarter's sales hit a record $54.23 billion, and Micron expects about $61.5 billion next quarter.
Over 75% of next year's chips are already promised to customers, with deals that last through 2030.
The average analyst price goal of about $1,562 is far above where the stock trades now.
bear: Nvidia, Micron's biggest customer, suddenly lost its CEO, which raises questions about future chip orders.
The stock is down about 20% in a month and far below its 52-week high of about $1,255.
Micron's finance chief said memory price increases should slow down next year.
